title: Autonomy above A0 is issued only on the founder's signed AUTONOMY_GRANT for that exact subject, tuple and level (acceptance I.G5)
problem: On #196 f383fd26, AutonomyAuthority.issue(subject, tuple_, level=8, authorized_by='Alfonso Lopez') returned an active A8 license: the authorizer was a caller-supplied string, so any caller could type the founder's name and start an exact tuple at A1-A8, skipping the ten-criterion promotion ladder. The method's own docstring named binding A1+ issuance to a founder-signed envelope (greg/founder.py) as the open step; acceptance/missions.json I.G5 records the same gap as OPEN and buildable now.
founder_intent_refs: acceptance/missions.json I.G5 (section 33, mission I: attack containment)
docs/FOUNDER_EFFECT_COMPILER.md: intelligence never creates authority; no component may authorize its own promotion
AGENTS.md: Alfonso is root authority; implementation creates no deployment or consequence authority
baseline: #196 claude/greg-full-machine-completion-whgiee at f383fd26: a name alone issued A8 (reproduced in this session); the existing tests issued A1+ with authorized_by='Alfonso Lopez' and no signature.

alternatives.name: Signed AUTONOMY_GRANT checked by the existing FounderVerifier (chosen)
alternatives.description: Add one founder-only command kind; AutonomyAuthority takes a verifier and, above A0, verifies a grant whose body is exactly {subject, tuple, level}, refuses a spent nonce, and records key id, nonce and envelope digest.
advantages: reuses the one founder-signature verifier, so no second authentication path
binds the exact tuple and level, so a grant for A2 cannot start A5
fails closed: no verifier, no A1+
disadvantages: one more command kind in greg/founder.py
no Body command path or CLI signer yet: the authority is a library

alternatives.name: Reuse DECISION envelopes
alternatives.description: Accept a founder-signed DECISION whose body names the tuple.
disadvantages: a DECISION answers a pending request on a body; overloading it lets an answer to one ask be replayed as an autonomy grant
alternatives.revival_evidence: if command kinds become a scarce, governed resource

alternatives.name: Remove issuance above A0 entirely
alternatives.description: Every license starts at A0 and climbs only through promote.
disadvantages: removes the founder's stated ability to start a bounded tuple above A0; the docstring and #87 keep it as a founder grant
alternatives.revival_evidence: the founder rules that starting levels above A0 should not exist

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: Any caller that types a human name starts any exact tuple at up to A8.
disadvantages: I.G5 stays open; the ladder stays optional through its constructor
the authorizer field claims an authentication it does not perform

roles.position: Advances 'no component may authorize its own promotion' and I.G5's next step as written; it narrows who can start autonomy and grants nothing.
material_concerns: the founder still has no CLI command to sign a grant; until one exists he can only sign with sign_command

roles.position: One verifier (greg.founder.FounderVerifier), one new kind, one helper in AutonomyAuthority; the autonomy package gains a lazy import of greg.founder (no new two-way package edge; test_import_layering passes).
material_concerns: autonomy -> greg dependency direction; acceptable because greg owns founder authentication

roles.position: Attacked with: a name alone, an unenrolled key, a delegated device key, a device that somehow lists the kind, another subject/tuple/level/budget/environment/action, the wrong kind, another body, an expired grant, a grant edited after signing, a replay, junk authorization, UNIIMENTE named with a valid grant, A9 with a grant. Every case is refused before anything is stored and has a test; 8/8 mutants of the safeguards are caught.
material_concerns: replay is checked only against this authority's own ledger: two authorities on two ledgers could each spend one grant

roles.position: Callers must now hold a verifier; the only runtime caller is the closure probe set, which uses a per-probe throwaway key labelled as synthetic. One fast mutation gate joins job 10b.
material_concerns: future callers that forget the verifier get a clear refusal, not silent A0

roles.position: Evidence tier is UNIT: the library is exercised with real Ed25519 keys in-process; no GREG Body path, no founder device, no founder grant exists. The record says so in I.G5's closed_by.
material_concerns: closing I.G5 at unit tier could be read as body-tier closure

evidence.claim: a name alone issued A8 before the change
evidence.finding: issue('agent-1', t, level=8, authorized_by='Alfonso Lopez') -> A8 active
24 passed; the file does not import on f383fd26 (no GRANT_KIND)

counterevidence.finding: a grant is refused a second time on the same authority's ledger; nothing prevents a second authority on a separate ledger from honouring it once more (the verifier's seen_nonce is the caller's to back)

pass_1.intended_outcome: No exact tuple starts above A0 unless Alfonso's enrolled key signed that grant; everything else still climbs only through the promotion ladder.

advantages.statement: the authorizer field now records an authentication, not a claim
advantages.amplified_value: autonomy.issued carries founder_key_id, nonce and envelope digest, so any later reader can re-verify
a grant for one tuple and level cannot be stretched to another

disadvantages.statement: no Body command path or CLI signer: the founder must sign with sign_command
disadvantages.redesigned_response: recorded as the residual in I.G5's closed_by and in the PR's next requirement; the body refuses an AUTONOMY_GRANT dropped in its inbox as an unsupported kind rather than mis-handling it
the verifier's seen_nonce stays caller-backed; a body-integrated authority will back it with the body ledger like every other command

disadvantages.statement: existing callers and tests must change
disadvantages.redesigned_response: one helper per caller; probes use a labelled throwaway key and never the founder's name

comparisons.baseline: name-only issuance, A8 reachable by any caller
comparisons.simplest_viable_alternative: forbid A1+ issuance entirely (rejected: removes a founder power)
comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: route issuance through a Body command and the MissionBook (deferred: no runtime consumer needs it yet)
comparisons.reversible_experiment: draft PR into #196; revert restores the previous behaviour

rejected_alternatives.name: Reuse DECISION envelopes
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: an answer to a pending ask must not double as an autonomy grant
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: a ruling that command kinds must not grow

rejected_alternatives.name: Forbid A1+ issuance
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: removes a founder grant the design keeps
rejected_alternatives.revival_evidence: the founder rules starting levels above A0 out

pass_2.attack_summary: Re-attacked with the signature in place: a device key whose delegation listed the kind (only possible if DEVICE_KINDS were widened) would pass verify, so the explicit founder-principal check is kept and a test widens DEVICE_KINDS to prove it; a grant edited after signing fails verification; the name checks still run first so a valid grant cannot launder 'UNIIMENTE' as authorizer.

new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: lazy import inside the check; no new two-way package edge (test_import_layering passes)

new_weaknesses.statement: two inputs (authorized_by and authorization) for one grant
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: the docstring states their roles: the name is the human-readable label and still must pass the name checks; the signature is the authentication

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: no runtime consumer of A1+ licenses exists on the body; a CLI signer is the next requirement
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.owner: next session to take I.G5's body tier
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: the first body or CLI path that issues autonomy above A0

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: one authority per ledger is the only shape in the tree
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: a second AutonomyAuthority over a different ledger for the same subject

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: all callers updated in this change

pass_2.final_design: AUTONOMY_GRANT in greg.founder.COMMAND_KINDS (not DEVICE_KINDS); AutonomyAuthority(ledger, verifier=None); above A0, issue runs the name checks, then _verified_grant (verifier present, envelope verifies as AUTONOMY_GRANT, principal is the founder key, body equals {subject, tuple, level}, nonce unspent on this ledger), then records the signature summary; refusals store nothing.

residual_risks.risk: the founder has no CLI to sign a grant

dissent.handling: Kept here and in the PR body; nothing hidden in code.

entries.position: I.G5 could stay OPEN until a Body path issues autonomy
entries.rationale: the gap as written is about issuance being unsigned, which is now closed at the only issuance point; body integration is a new gap
entries.evidence_threshold: any path that issues A1+ without passing through AutonomyAuthority.issue

migration_plan: None for data: autonomy.issued records written before this change keep their name-only authorized_by; licenses are in-memory. Callers pass verifier= and authorization=.

steps: revert the commit on the branch
AUTONOMY_GRANT disappears from COMMAND_KINDS; no body ever accepted one

kill_criteria: any path issues A1+ without a verified founder AUTONOMY_GRANT
a device key's signature issues autonomy
a refusal leaves a license or an autonomy.issued record
the change breaks an existing promote/regress/renew behaviour
decision_owner: Alfonso Lopez for adoption onto main; the #196 integrator for intake
review_trigger: intake review on #196; the first runtime issuance of autonomy above A0
